paper.title: Accurate piezoelectric tensor prediction with equivariant attention tensor graph neural network
paper.research_summary: The paper proposes an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) to predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor for both bulk and two-dimensional materials, leveraging irreducible decomposition to preserve crystal symmetry and frame independence. It combines machine learning predictions with first-principles calculations to discover new high-performance piezoelectric materials.

task.objective: accurately predict the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor
constraints: must be independent of reference frame
output_goal: full third-rank piezoelectric tensor in Voigt notation

evidence.text: Here, we propose an equivariant attention tensor graph neural network (EATGNN) that can identify crystal symmetry and remain independent of the reference frame, ultimately enabling the accurate prediction of the complete third-rank piezoelectric tensor.

EATGNN can establish the relationship between crystal structures and their properties... Ultimately, the model outputs the piezoelectric tensor in its irreducible representation, which is then post-processed to obtain the target piezoelectric tensor.

stages.stage_goal: acquire piezoelectric tensor data for bulk and 2D materials

evidence.text: The piezoelectric tensor data of bulk crystals in this work was obtained from the Materials Project21 and a recent high-throughput computational study on piezoelectric tensors24,30.
The piezoelectric tensor data of 2D materials was obtained from the C2DB database33,34, comprising a total of 1382 data points...

stages.stage_goal: clean outliers and enforce crystal symmetry constraints on piezoelectric tensors

evidence.text: Due to the presence of a significant number of outliers in the piezoelectric tensors, we performed data resampling before applying machine learning techniques to prevent overfitting.
We mathematically adjusted those piezoelectric tensors that did not conform to the material’s symmetry to be invariant under crystallographic symmetry operations.

We first checked whether the piezoelectric tensors in the dataset satisfy the symmetry of their corresponding crystal structures... If a change occurred, we transformed the tensor into a symmetry-compliant form that respects the lattice symmetry.

stages.stage_name_raw: training EATGNN with MSE loss on piezoelectric tensor
stages.stage_goal: train equivariant graph neural network to predict piezoelectric tensor

evidence.text: Networks are trained using a mean-squared-error loss function based on complete piezoelectric tensor: loss = 1/N Σ Σ (e'ₙᵢⱼₖ − eₙᵢⱼₖ)² / 27

stages.stage_name_raw: performance evaluation using MAE and RMSE
stages.stage_goal: quantify prediction accuracy of piezoelectric tensor components

evidence.text: The Root Mean Squared Error (RMSE) and Mean Absolute Error (MAE) of EATGNN on the test set are 0.154 C/m2 and 0.141 C/m2, respectively.
the RMSE and MAE of our model are 50.6 pC/m and 16.8 pC/m, respectively.

stages.stage_goal: identify new materials with large predicted piezoelectricity

evidence.text: In order to discover new potential high-performance piezoelectric materials, we use our model on both 3D and 2D materials in the Materials Project and 2DMatPedia database36, respectively.

stages.stage_goal: validate predicted candidates using first-principles calculations

evidence.text: Our selection criteria are 1) out of the training datasets, 2) inversion asymmetry, 3) Egap > 0.1 eV, and 4) Nuc < 30 atoms. Using our model, we identify several good candidates (See in Tables 3 and 4 and Supplementary Material), which are further validated using density functional perturbation theory (DFPT) calculations.
